newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end higher on mainly local buying.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end higher on mainly local buying.

text.p: Malaysian shares closed in positive territory on Tuesday, supported by local institutional funds and retail players, said analysts.
At the close the key Composite Index of 100 leading stocks ended 8.86 points, or 0.79 percent, higher at 1,126.83. The broader EMAS index gained 1.85 points to end at 317.84.
"Most of the acquisitions have been by local funds. There has been no follow-through buying by foreign funds," said Irene Tan, research manager at brokers Vickers Ballas.
Volume rose to 255 million shares valued at 1,837 million ringgit. Losers outpaced gainers 305 to 246.

Companies linked to the Bakun hydro-electric dam project in Sarawak state were among the most active, mainly driven by speculative plays, analysts said. Ekran Bhd, the main promoter of the project, gained 30 cents to 5.75 ringgit.

Independent power producer YTL Power International ended six cents higher at 3.72. The company said on Monday it had received approval from Chinese state authorities to proceed with the acquisition of a power plant in Jiangxi province.
"There was an initial euphoria this morning, but it (YTL Power) is still overpriced," said Faez Khairuddin, head of research at S.J. Securities.
Shares of timber concern Jaya Tiasa surged after its requotation earlier in the morning, peaking at 15.10 ringgit. The stock rose two ringgit to 13.80 at the close.
On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange the spot June contract gained 12.5 points to end at 1,147.0, with 1,418 lots traded. No other contracts were traded.
